neighbours.label: 'know' as the verb of a how-can-I-tell question (How do I know if..., How can I know which...): asking for a way to find something out, not stating knowledge; also Korean 보 in 어떻게 보 questions
fire: My tomato leaves are curling. How do I know if the plant has a fungus?
We bought a used car last month. How can I know whether the mileage is real?
The baby cries a lot at night. How do you know when she is actually hungry?
I'm new to baking bread. How will I know when the dough has risen enough?
The router blinks orange. How do I know which light means no connection?
There are three keys on the ring. How can I know which one opens the shed?
I've never had my eyes tested. How do I know if I need glasses?
My dog keeps scratching. How can we know if he has fleas?
quiet: My tomato leaves are curling. I know the plant needs more water.
We bought a used car last month. How can I check whether the mileage is real?
The baby cries a lot at night. Do you know a good lullaby?
I'm new to baking bread. How will I tell when the dough has risen enough?
The router blinks orange. I know that light means no connection.
There are three keys on the ring. How can I find which one opens the shed?
I've never had my eyes tested. Everyone knows I need glasses.
My dog keeps scratching. How can we find out if he has fleas?
